feature: A set of titles that look designed
summary: The Library's Comps shelf and the Insert menus now offer twelve titles built to the research brief instead of the eight plain ones: nine title pages and three lower thirds, each with its parts on separate beats, words that come in by line, word or letter, and something still moving while it holds.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Open a recording and show the Library in the dock.

try.do: In the Library, pick Comps and point at a few title tiles: each one plays its in, a hold and its way off.
Double click Keynote Clean, type a title and press Command Return.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Do these read as designed by a motion designer, rather than as slides?
Is there one you would use on your next screen recording as it comes, without touching a knob?
Do Minimal Underline's words read well enough over a bright, busy screenshot?
Are three lower thirds enough, or do you want more name cards than title pages?
Should By and Stagger live only in the Part section, now that the Reveal section below it edits the same words?
rough: No mock draws these presets; the twelve style directions in docs/design/video-titles-polish.md are the spec, and every one of them is built.

The soft whoosh and tick sounds the brief asked for are not here: the app has no sound clips to use (its sound effects are EQ, Compressor and Noise reduction), so they are their own task, titles-can-play-a-soft-whoosh-and-tick-as-they-b.
Kinetic Bold keeps one colour behind its words; the brief's colour that swaps on each word beat is left out, since a swap keyed by hand would stop the theme recolouring it.
Tech Terminal has no scanlines or grid and no letter scramble before each letter locks: the app draws neither yet.
Light Leak and Kinetic Bold are drawn in capitals, but words you type keep the case you type them in; there is no capitals setting on text.
Editorial Serif's kicker is not tracked wide (+0.15em), because text has no letter spacing setting; it is small semibold capitals instead.
Behind Glass dims the recording by 55% rather than the brief's 40%, so its white words read over a white screenshot.
Minimal Underline sits on a soft dark shade rather than nothing, so it stays legible over a light recording; over a busy light screenshot it is readable but not crisp.
Gradient Glow's Part menu lists its gradient and its glowing headline as Accent 1 and Accent 2, which says little about which is which.

The Part section's By and Stagger and the Reveal section under it both set how a title's words come in; a reveal set in the Reveal section now survives turning any title knob, until that part's In is changed.
Name cards are three of twelve, the brief's three lower thirds; the old rule of four per kind was relaxed to three.
